sources.text: D ata I ntelligence V alues E thics R esearch The DIVER lab studies the intersection of data, cognition, and values, using methods from philosophy, psychology, machine learning, and public policy. Research areas in the DIVER lab include: Algorithmic bias discovery & mitigation Ethical analyses of emerging technologies Policy design challenges for emerging technologies Goal & value influences on human cognition Causal discovery from observational and experimental data Time series analysis from complex measurements If you are interested in joining the DIVER lab (or if you are a prospective graduate student), please read these FAQs before contacting Prof. Danks. Due to funding constraints & cut-backs, I am highly unlikely to admit any new Ph.D. students in Data Science for Fall 2027 . (But I am open to collaboration with current UVA students.)

sources.title: About — David Danks
sources.text: I am the William L. Polk Jr. and Carolyn K. Polk Jefferson Scholars Foundation Distinguished University Professor of Philosophy , Artificial Intelligence , & Data Science at University of Virginia . I have had the honor of serving on advisory boards for various organizations including: National AI Advisory Committee (NAIAC) Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP) Computer Science & Telecommunications Board (National Academies) Partnership to Advance Responsible Technology (PART) Topos Institute I have been named a James S. McDonnell Foundation Scholar (2008); an Andrew Carnegie Fellow (2017); and a Schmidt Sciences AI2050 Senior Fellow (2026). Previously, I was Professor of Data Science , Philosophy , & Policy at University of California, San Diego ,. Before that, I was the L.L. Thurstone Professor of Philosophy & Psychology at Carnegie Mellon University . While at CMU, I served as the Chief Ethicist of CMU’s Block Center for Technology & Society and co-director of CMU’s Center for Informed Democracy and Social Cybersecurity (IDeaS) My research interests are at the intersection of philosophy, cognitive science, and machine learning, using ideas, methods, and frameworks from each to advance our understanding of complex, interdisciplinary problems. I have explored the ethical, psychological, and policy issues around AI and robotics in transportation, healthcare, privacy, and security. I have done significant research in computational cognitive science. And I have developed multiple novel causal discovery algorithms for complex types of observational and experimental data.
